target_customer: Employers such as school districts, colleges and hospitals funding homeownership programs for staff in high cost markets
problem: Teachers and essential workers cannot afford a down payment in expensive housing markets.
business_model: Shared appreciation down payment: Landed funds part of the down payment and shares in the home's appreciation or depreciation; later white label employer programs
product_category: Proptech and fintech, down payment assistance

founders.name: Jonathan Asmis
founders.background_notes: YC page: began as a biomedical engineer making vaccines, then worked on social impact bonds and securitizing energy storage revenues

founders.name: Jesse Vaughan
founders.background_notes: Named as a 2015 co-founder on Landed's website

technical_complexity.rationale: Application and underwriting software; the hard part was raising institutional capital for the down payment pool.

defensibility.rationale: Employer partnerships and a funded capital pool, though shared equity products from others existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition by a larger player was found; the company's own site says governments took over its work in California and Colorado and it refocused on education and healthcare employers.

market_need_then: Not independently sourced for 2015 to 2016; later coverage describes teachers and essential workers priced out of homeownership.

branding.domain_note: Company site is landed.com; no purchase history found.

brand_strength.rationale: A simple evocative word and strong cause marketing for teachers, but no evidence the name itself drove growth.

pivots.from: Consumer shared appreciation down payments for teachers
pivots.to: White label employer funded housing benefit programs for education and healthcare staff
pivots.why: Company says rising interest rates and falling private appetite for long term housing investment, and governments taking over its work in California and Colorado (date not stated).

outcome_analysis: Landed raised a 7.5M Series A in 2019, a 10.5M extension in 2020 and a 31M Series B in 2021 to fund a shared appreciation down payment program for educators. When rates rose and private investors lost interest in long term housing exposure it shifted to employer funded programs. The YC directory marks it Acquired but no acquisition could be found and the company still operates under its own name, so the exit status is unresolved.
notes: YC status says Acquired but two outcome searches and the company site show no acquirer; exit.type is unknown and this conflicts with the directory. Earlier investors named without dates (Lowe's Ventures, Ulu Ventures, YC, Clocktower) are not recorded as rounds. Landed also raised over 50M USD of private real estate capital for the down payment pool, which is not venture funding. Aggregator totals vary (53M to 62M); unverified. Unsourced claims of 2026 program pauses were ignored. Competitor sources (Unison, Point) were undated, so the list is empty.
